documents.unit: Compass 2035 / AI at Smith Art of Inquiry
documents.title: AI at Smith: Students
documents.stance_why: The page says 'Policies vary by course and professor' and tells students to 'know your course policy' and ask when in doubt, so the college sets no AI rule itself and hands the decision to professors, which is delegates.
documents.summary: Student-facing page of five expectations for generative AI at Smith: know the course policy, disclose and cite, verify, guard data, and embrace difficulty, plus support resources. It sets no college-wide ban or permission and defers to each course.

units.why: The heading and its first bullet say 'Policies vary by course and professor', which places the AI decision with each professor rather than one college rule, so it is P04 (not P11, which is about non-carryover).
units.anchor: Policies vary by course and professor

units.why: The heading 'Know your course policy' tells students it is their job to find out the rules for each course, which is P78; P10 (ask when unsure) is a separate bullet.
units.anchor: Know your course policy
units.policy: Students know their course's AI policy.

units.why: 'When in doubt, ask your professor before using AI for a class project' is the ask-first rule in P10, addressed to students and tied to doing coursework.
units.anchor: When in doubt, ask your professor before using AI for a class project
units.frag_end: using AI for a class project

units.why: 'Ask proactively to discuss course expectations and whether AI tools should be part of that process' asks students to start the conversation with the professor; closest is P10, but it goes beyond unsureness to proactively opening a discussion.
units.anchor: Ask proactively to discuss course expectations and whether AI tools should be part
units.fit_note: Students are told to proactively open a discussion about expectations and whether AI should be part of the course process, not only to ask when unsure.

units.why: 'Cite and disclose AI use like other outside sources' requires acknowledgment of AI use as with any outside source, so P24; the 'like other outside sources' comparison is secondary to the disclosure duty.
units.anchor: Cite and disclose AI use like other outside sources

units.why: 'Document prompts and tool contributions' asks students to record the prompts and what the tool contributed, which is the prompt/tool detail of P25 rather than full transcripts (P26).
units.anchor: Document prompts and tool contributions

units.why: 'Demonstrate your own thinking so your professors can respond to you and help you learn' keeps the student as the visible thinker, which is P32; the purpose is so professors can respond.
units.anchor: Demonstrate your own thinking so your professors can respond to you

units.why: 'Keep a human in the loop and check AI-generated information before sharing' tells students to verify AI output, so P31.
units.anchor: Keep a human in the loop and check AI-generated information before sharing

units.why: 'Verify claims and check sources' with the reason 'AI tools predict language patterns, not facts' is a verify-output rule with a stated reason, P31.
units.anchor: Verify claims and check sources
units.policy: Students verify claims and check sources because AI tools predict language patterns, not facts.

units.why: 'Misinformation is always possible—treat responses as a starting point' warns that AI output can be wrong and should not be accepted as final, P31 (sibling bullet to the verify rule, a different point: treat output as a draft).
units.anchor: Misinformation is always possible—treat responses as a starting point

units.why: 'Protect personal information and sensitive research data' is a data-protection duty for students, P50.
units.anchor: Protect personal information and sensitive research data

units.why: 'Never enter private data in public unsupported AI platforms' is a flat prohibition on private data in unsupported tools, P50 (data protection and tool vetting).
units.anchor: Never enter private data in public unsupported AI platforms

units.why: 'Google Workspace is college approved—use Google Gemini and Notebook with your Smith ID' points students to the college-approved tools, which is P92 (institution-wide tools, not a single course).
units.anchor: Google Workspace is college approved—use Google Gemini and Notebook with your Smith ID
units.frag_end: with your Smith ID to protect your data
units.policy: Google Workspace is college approved; students use Google Gemini and Notebook with their Smith ID to protect their data.

units.why: 'Seek out friction in the learning process—wrestling with ideas supports real cognitive growth' gives desirable difficulty as a reason to do the thinking yourself, P41.
units.anchor: Seek out friction in the learning process

units.why: 'Cultivate your own unique voice to say the things that only you can say' asks students to develop their own voice; no type covers voice or perspective as a goal (P32 is about being the problem-solver), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Cultivate your own unique voice to say the things that only you can say
units.uncovered_note: Students are urged to cultivate their own unique voice and perspective rather than outsourcing it to AI.

units.why: 'Interns will provide AI training to students and coordinate a series of student-to-student outreach activities' describes institution-provided AI training for students, P70.
units.anchor: Interns will provide AI training to students
units.frag_end: conversations around AI and higher education.
units.policy: ITS runs a student-led AI internship program whose interns provide AI training to students and coordinate student-to-student outreach on AI and higher education.

units.why: The Jacobson Center is listed for 'writing guidance, brainstorming, planning, and support for revising your writing', directing students to human writing support, P72.
units.anchor: For writing guidance, brainstorming, planning, and support for revising your writing.

units.why: 'Work with Subject Librarians to find authoritative and reliable sources' points students to human librarians for source-finding, P72.
units.anchor: Work with Subject Librarians to find authoritative and reliable sources.

units.why: 'Reach out to your professors or class dean when feeling uncertain about policies or overwhelmed by coursework' directs students to human help; P72 fits, although the 'overwhelmed' part also touches P99.
units.anchor: Reach out to your professors or class dean when feeling uncertain about policies
units.fit_note: Also names being overwhelmed by coursework as a reason to seek help, which touches reducing pressure that leads to misuse (P99).

units.why: The AI Literacy Research Guide offers 'more information about AI technologies, ethics, research, and criticism', a guide for AI literacy, P70.
units.anchor: Find more information about AI technologies, ethics, research, and criticism.

documents.title: AI at Smith: Faculty and Staff
documents.stance_why: The page offers 'tailored documents intended to help inform AI decisions in the classroom' and a video to 'facilitate course discussions', and sets no student AI rule, so it hands decisions to instructors: delegates.
documents.summary: Faculty and staff overview of AI at Smith: the AI Steering Committee, resources for educators, approved tools (Gemini and Notebook), a course pilot platform, training, and a data security review. It gives instructors resources rather than a course rule.

units.why: It says 'the AI Steering Committee and working groups are leading efforts to provide clear, thoughtful guidance', naming the bodies that own the guidance, P80.
units.anchor: the AI Steering Committee and working groups
units.policy: The AI Steering Committee and working groups lead efforts to provide guidance on using AI responsibly at Smith.

units.why: The sentence sets the scope of the guidance, 'responsibly at Smith, whether that's in teaching, research, administration, or operations', a framework statement P56; the committee in the same sentence is coded separately as P80.
units.anchor: guidance on using AI responsibly at Smith, whether that’s in teaching, research, administration, or operations
units.policy: The college provides clear, thoughtful guidance on using AI responsibly at Smith in teaching, research, administration and operations.

units.why: 'Smith faculty and staff are actively exploring how artificial intelligence can enhance learning, spark creativity, and streamline daily work' names benefits of AI without making a rule, P87.
units.anchor: how artificial intelligence can enhance learning, spark creativity, and streamline daily work

units.why: 'committed to helping members of the Smith community make confident, informed decisions around engaging with AI tools' states the institution's support commitment as part of its framework; P56 is nearest but it is about a commitment to support rather than purpose or scope.
units.anchor: committed to helping members of the Smith community make confident, informed decisions
units.policy: The college is committed to helping members of the Smith community make confident, informed decisions around engaging with AI tools.
units.fit_note: A commitment to support informed decision-making, rather than a statement of purpose, scope or principles.

units.why: 'We prioritize the protection of data and privacy' is the college stating privacy as a priority principle, P50.
units.anchor: We prioritize the protection of data and privacy

units.why: 'maintaining the accuracy and integrity of any content created with assistance from AI' puts a duty on faculty and staff to keep AI-assisted content accurate, P31 (verify output).
units.anchor: maintaining the accuracy and integrity of any content created with assistance from AI
units.policy: Faculty and staff maintain the accuracy and integrity of any content created with assistance from AI.
units.fit_note: Addressed to faculty and staff about their own AI-assisted content.

units.why: 'these tools support, not replace, the original work and critical thinking of the faculty and staff' keeps humans as the primary thinkers; P32 is nearest although it is written about faculty and staff, not students.
units.anchor: these tools support, not replace, the original work and critical thinking
units.fit_note: Applies to faculty and staff rather than students.

units.why: 'a new video resource will be available to use as a tool to facilitate course discussions on the use of generative AI' gives instructors a means to discuss AI rules with students, P66.
units.anchor: a new video resource will be available to use as a tool to facilitate course
units.frag_start: This fall, a new video resource

units.why: The video covers 'the importance of understanding course-specific syllabus policies', telling students to learn each course's rules, P78.
units.anchor: the importance of understanding course-specific syllabus policies
units.policy: The video covers the importance of understanding course-specific syllabus policies.

units.why: The video emphasizes 'our students' authentic intellectual development and encouraging their responsible exploration of these technologies', a statement of benefits and purpose, P87; no rule is given.
units.anchor: authentic intellectual development and encouraging their responsible exploration of these technologies
units.policy: The video emphasizes students' authentic intellectual development and encourages their responsible exploration of generative AI technologies.
units.fit_note: Pairs authentic intellectual development with encouraging responsible exploration; P87 captures only the benefit side.

units.why: 'a set of tailored documents intended to help inform AI decisions in the classroom' is support for instructors setting course policy, P63.
units.anchor: a set of tailored documents intended to help inform AI decisions in the classroom

units.why: 'Departments across the college are identifying potential ways to leverage enterprise-wide AI tools' is about AI in operations, not teaching, so P76.
units.anchor: Departments across the college are identifying potential ways to leverage enterprise-wide AI tools

units.why: 'Smith College has approved specific AI tools, including Google Gemini and Notebook, for general use by faculty and staff' names the approved institution-wide tools, P92.
units.anchor: Smith College has approved specific AI tools, including Google Gemini and Notebook

units.why: 'Smith ITS provides guidance and resources for the use of AI tools', including instructions, use cases and privacy information, is staff support in learning AI, P63.
units.anchor: Smith ITS provides guidance and resources for the use of AI tools

units.why: 'a platform that enables faculty and students in their courses to experiment with industry-leading AI tools, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's GPT models' is a college-provided tool for courses, P17.
units.anchor: Smith is also piloting a platform that enables faculty and students in their courses

units.why: 'interactive training sessions and workshops held by the ITS department' offer employees AI training, P63 (faculty and staff support; P70 is for wider audiences).
units.anchor: interactive training sessions and workshops held by the ITS department
units.frag_end: campus AI tools in their work.

units.why: 'Submit a request for an AI tool data security review' is a review process before enabling a tool for work, P65.
units.anchor: request for an AI tool data security review
units.policy: Anyone hoping to enable an AI tool for work submits a request for an AI tool data security review.

units.why: 'Confidential data cannot be used in AI tools unless the CIO/Counsel has made an exception' bans confidential data in AI tools; the exception route is part of the same rule, so P50 not P80.
units.anchor: Confidential data cannot be used in AI tools unless the CIO/Counsel has made an exception

documents.title: Academic Integrity Board Information for Faculty
documents.stance_why: The Board says 'make decisions about what you will allow in a given course' and 'state exactly whether and how students are allowed to use this technology in your course', so it does not fix a stance and hands the decision to instructors: delegates.
documents.summary: Academic Integrity Board FAQ and advice for faculty on suspected violations, including generative AI, AI detectors, and how to set and communicate course policy. It says instructors must state their AI rules and that the Board does not rely on detectors.

units.why: 'Invite the student to talk about the situation. Approach the conversation non-judgmentally' tells instructors to talk with the student before reporting, P57.
units.anchor: Invite the student to talk about the situation.
units.policy: Instructors invite the student to talk about the situation and approach the conversation non-judgmentally and with an open mind.

units.why: 'you should never rely on this software to prove that a student has used generative AI' bans using AI detectors as proof, P39.
units.anchor: you should never rely on this software to prove that a student has used
units.frag_start: For this reason, you should never

units.why: 'The AIB does not rely on the results of AI-detecting software to make decisions about cases' states the Board's own practice, P39.
units.anchor: The AIB does not rely on the results of AI-detecting software

units.why: The page says detector work 'by certain people, like non-native English speakers and those who are neurodivergent, is more likely to yield false positives', giving the reason detectors are unreliable and biased; P39 is the unreliability type, though this adds a bias point.
units.anchor: non-native English speakers and those who are neurodivergent, is more likely to yield false positives
units.frag_end: wrongfully identified as generated by AI).
units.fit_note: Adds that detectors are biased against non-native English speakers and neurodivergent people.

units.why: '“Proving” that the work ... was actually generated by AI is not a straightforward task' admits AI use is hard to verify, P82.
units.anchor: was actually generated by AI is not a straightforward task.

units.why: 'We strongly encourage faculty members to learn about the limitations of AI-detecting software' tells faculty to stay informed about a specific AI issue, P102.
units.anchor: We strongly encourage faculty members to learn about the limitations of AI-detecting software
units.frag_start: We strongly encourage faculty members to

units.why: 'The AIB strongly encourages faculty to submit all cases of suspected violations to the Board' is the formal reporting step, P81; it is generic to integrity cases on a page that also handles AI cases.
units.anchor: The AIB strongly encourages faculty to submit all cases of suspected violations to the Board.
units.frag_start: The AIB strongly encourages faculty to

units.why: 'it is simply unfair to students when some faculty are more likely to report cases than others' grounds reporting in fairness, P95.
units.anchor: it is simply unfair to students when some faculty are more likely to report cases
units.frag_start: From an equity standpoint, it is

units.why: 'the AIB is driven not by a punitive mandate, but by an educational mandate' frames the response as educative, P68.
units.anchor: the AIB is driven not by a punitive mandate, but by an educational mandate

units.why: 'the Board’s most common sanction is to lower the grade on the piece of coursework in question' states the usual penalty in advance, P37.
units.anchor: most common sanction is to lower the grade on the piece of coursework in question

units.why: 'The most important thing you can do is to make your expectations and course policies clear on your course's syllabus' requires AI expectations on the syllabus, P09, as part of the AI/integrity guidance.
units.anchor: make your expectations and course policies clear on your course’s syllabus

units.why: 'You also can give specific guidelines for specific assignments, especially if the expectations vary across assignments' lets rules be set per assignment, P04.
units.anchor: You also can give specific guidelines for specific assignments

units.why: 'Be sure that you state exactly whether and how students are allowed to use this technology in your course' requires instructors to state their AI rule, P09.
units.anchor: state exactly whether and how students are allowed to use this technology in your course.
units.frag_end: use this technology in your course.

units.why: 'Reinforce those expectations every time students are working on an assignment' asks for repeated reminders; P09 is nearest, but it goes beyond stating the rule once.
units.anchor: Reinforce those expectations every time students are working on an assignment
units.fit_note: Asks instructors to repeat the AI expectations at each assignment, beyond a single syllabus statement.

units.why: 'students can make erroneous assumptions in cases where no expectations about the use of generative AI are stated on the syllabus' is the reason for stating rules; it does not set a fallback, so P09 not P06.
units.anchor: students can make erroneous assumptions in cases where no expectations about the use

units.why: 'speak with students about the importance of academic honesty for the learning process', with 'discipline-specific conversations at the beginning of the semester', asks instructors to explain and discuss the rules, P66.
units.anchor: speak with students about the importance of academic honesty for the learning process
units.frag_start: In addition to stating course policies

units.why: 'The Academic Integrity Board has seen an increase in cases regarding the use of generative AI' gives evidence about AI and integrity, P55 (evidence collected); it is data, not a rule.
units.anchor: has seen an increase in cases regarding the use of generative AI.
units.frag_start: The Academic Integrity Board has seen
units.fit_note: Reports case counts rather than evidence on learning or performance.

units.why: 'Students are using generative AI as learners in many ways: as a study partner, to generate quiz questions, to hear alternative explanations of concepts, to summarize readings' lists acceptable learner uses; closest is P14 (study aids), though it also covers explanation and summarizing.
units.anchor: as a study partner, to generate quiz questions, to hear alternative explanations of concepts
units.frag_start: Students are using generative AI as
units.fit_note: Also includes hearing alternative explanations of concepts (P12) and summarizing readings, and describes use rather than granting permission.

units.why: 'The AIB encourages instructors to learn about the ways that students use generative AI and make decisions about what you will allow in a given course' leaves the choice to instructors, P04.
units.anchor: make decisions about what you will allow in a given course
units.frag_start: The AIB encourages instructors to learn

units.why: 'if your course focuses on building students' critical reading skills, you might state that students are not allowed to use generative AI to summarize course readings' ties the rule to learning objectives, P83.
units.anchor: if your course focuses on building students’ critical reading skills
units.frag_start: For example, if your course focuses
units.policy: If a course focuses on building critical reading skills, the instructor might state that students may not use generative AI to summarize course readings.

units.why: 'speak with students about the importance of developing one's own voice as a writer' asks instructors to discuss the point with students, P66.
units.anchor: speak with students about the importance of developing one’s own voice as a writer.
units.frag_start: The AIB encourages faculty to speak

units.why: 'Using generative AI to write a paper removes an opportunity to develop that voice' gives the skill-building reason for limiting AI writing, P41.
units.anchor: Using generative AI to write a paper removes an opportunity to develop that voice.

units.why: 'It is the student's voice we want to hear, not the voice of generative AI' says the work should be the student's own; P32 is nearest but it is about voice rather than problem-solving.
units.anchor: It is the student’s voice we want to hear, not the voice of generative AI.
units.fit_note: Concerns the student's own voice as writer rather than being the primary problem-solver.

units.why: 'Talk with your students about what is sacrificed if they use AI to substitute for their own thinking' tells instructors to discuss the costs of substituting AI for thinking, P66.
units.anchor: Talk with your students about what is sacrificed if they use AI to substitute
units.frag_start: Talk with your students about what

units.why: 'please consider sharing your assignments with colleagues' invites faculty to share strategies for teaching responsible AI use, P63 (faculty community).
units.anchor: please consider sharing your assignments with colleagues
units.frag_start: If you are committed to teaching
units.fit_note: Peer sharing among faculty of assignments for teaching responsible generative AI use.

notes: Coder B. The AIB page's reporting and sanction passages are generic integrity guidance but sit on a page that handles generative AI cases, so they were coded. The students page does not itself say AI is assumed not allowed; only the quoted text was coded. Course layer deferred; no computing-unit policy found.
